fills.fill: Man, he arose in his living power
fills.notes: Opening cosmogonic move: the First Man rises/stands forth and then delegates. Oldest-layer register is impersonal: a state-change, not exhortation.

fills.fill: sons, and he appointed over them
fills.notes: The syntax demands delegation: leadership given to five sons, then a further appointment/ordering involving Living Spirit and Mother of Life as ruling powers.
The next clause explains that “the entire ruling-power is entwined and crucified”; this points to the paired powers acting as the binding/ruling principle in the mixture.

fills.fill: in the mixture of the limbs
fills.notes: “Entwined and crucified” correspondentially marks extension/expansion into ultimates (limbs/members) and fixation there; this is the standard description of Light bound in the mixed creation.

fills.fill: took from him the measures of the mixture
fills.notes: The Living Spirit’s act here is technical: measuring/ordering the mingled substances before fashioning the ‘garments’ (cosmic structures).

fills.fill: from the darkness that had been taken captive
fills.notes: Garments/firmaments are constructed from the subdued dark matter; this keeps the oldest-layer cosmotechnical tone.
The repeated later clause “of the Father of Life [...] he set up all things” implies an earlier mention grounding the work in the Father-of-Life’s wisdom/power.
Delegation logic: the son receives leadership; the hanging/setting-up is performed under higher command/order.
Garments are ‘hung’ and ‘set up’ above/between regions; “in the height” matches the cosmological architecture register.
The phrase “of the Father of Life” naturally takes “wisdom/understanding” as genitive content in this layer (technical craftsmanship of the cosmos).
“He set up all things” typically means establishing limits, measures, and stations—correspondentially, the ordering of degrees and spaces.
After “he opened [...] ten firmaments” the next expected object is openings/gates/doors through the firmaments for ascents/descents of powers and lights.
Sequence: ten firmaments → wheel of the stars → luminaries/planets; these are the visible regulators of times and separations.
The simile needs a general artisan figure before “and an architect”; oldest-layer likes paired craft-images for ordering/formation.
Architect divides a royal dwelling into discrete rooms; ‘chambers’ keeps the palace-cosmos correspondence tighter than a vaguer ‘things’.
“everything that is required for beauty [...] and he cleans them” points to adornment/finishing work of ordered structures.
After furnishing/adornment and cleansing, the craftsman’s act is arranging into harmony so the king may inhabit; corresponds to cosmological ordering.

fills.fill: who takes a piece of wood
fills.notes: The carpenter simile requires the material (wood) as given before ‘before it was worked’.
Fits the tool-sequence later (plane, smoothing) and the progression from raw to finished.
“established and made beautiful” implies joining/setting; fitting precedes establishment.
The contrast is between raw wood and what is brought forth by art/skill; keeps the impersonal technical register.
Opposition: the finished form is not ‘in’ the wood externally yet; it exists in the artisan’s mind/understanding.
Sets up “in him in his [...] in his understanding”: the form pre-exists inwardly in the craftsman (correspondence: archetype in wisdom).
Triad: within him in his thought and in his understanding; standard pairing for interior design/plan.
After “cuts it into separate pieces [...] it” the missing verb is a second action like splitting/cleaving, matching carpentry process.
“he pulls the [...] it with the plane” naturally takes “shavings” as what is pulled off by planing.
Connects “pulls the shavings from it”; grammatical connector in the description.
Transition from carpenter-work to cosmic work: Father of Life ‘forms’/‘fashions’ the cosmos as an ordered dwelling.
“in limbs [...] palace” suggests the cosmos as a body with members; ‘great body’ matches correspondential body-palace analogy.
Explicitly carries the palace analogy: the cosmos is a dwelling prepared for the ‘great king’ (Third Ambassador).
“in it or in a [...] useful” points to smaller ‘implements’: vessel fits both carpentry list and cosmological ‘ships of light’.
“useful [...] the ships of light” calls for functional/service language: these structures serve the work of separation/ascent.
Alongside ‘ships of light’ and ‘other works’, ‘stations’ (places/standings of powers) is expected cosmological architecture vocabulary.
Locates the works: ships and stations operate through/within firmaments; matches earlier ‘ten firmaments’.
Purpose clause: prepared so that when the great king comes he may dwell; ‘prepared’ keeps the palace-building correspondence.

fills.fill: is to come forth in the last separation
fills.notes: The Third Ambassador’s appearing is tied to the great separation/judgment of mixture; oldest-layer phrasing avoids Christian coloring.
Completes the palace simile explicitly: universe as palace/dwelling for the royal presence.

fills.fill: the one who separates is the great Mind that is called the Just Judge
fills.notes: Line describes discriminating light from waste/darkness and consigning the latter to abyss; oldest-layer needs an impersonal separating faculty (Mind/Judge), not pastoral salvation language.

assessment: Most gaps can be constrained by the internal craft/palace correspondence (ordering, measuring, hanging firmaments, gates, luminaries) and by the standard cosmogonic sequence (mixture → construction of firmaments/garments → preparation of a cosmic dwelling → final separation). Exact wording remains tentative where the Coptic Vorlage could have used several near-synonyms (measure/boundary/station; thought/plan/understanding), but the demanded functions are stable and guide the restorations tightly.
